title: What Is a Swap?
subtitle: Two parties exchange future cash flows according to an agreed formula
openingQuestion: What is the core concept behind every type of swap?
openingOptions: It only applies to foreign currency
Two parties exchange a series of future cash flows
A swap always has a term under 1 year
Two parties exchange physical assets with each other directly
explanation: A swap is a derivative contract in which two parties agree to exchange future cash flows according to a predetermined formula. Most common: an Interest Rate Swap (swapping fixed-rate and floating-rate cash flows) and a Currency Swap (swapping cash flows in two different currencies). A swap lets each side convert the type of risk they carry into the type they'd rather have.

Swap future cash flows with each other

realWorldExample.description: The global Interest Rate Swap market has a notional value running into the hundreds of trillions of USD - one of the largest OTC derivatives markets in the world, mostly between banks and large corporations.

quiz.question: Is the notional principal in a swap contract actually exchanged between the two parties?
options: No, because notional is just a number written into a template contract
Yes, the two parties exchange the entire principal as soon as the contract is signed
Yes, but only once, exchanged on the maturity date
No, it is only the basis for calculating the interest each side owes the other
quiz.explanation: In an ordinary Interest Rate Swap, the notional principal (e.g. VND 100 billion) does not change hands - it is only the basis for calculating the fixed and floating interest each side owes the other. At the end of each period, only the difference (net) is actually settled, significantly reducing counterparty risk compared with exchanging the full notional.

quiz.question: If market interest rates move very sharply during the life of a swap contract, who benefits and who is disadvantaged in a typical Interest Rate Swap (one side pays fixed, the other pays floating)?
options: The fixed-rate payer benefits when rates rise, loses when rates fall
Both sides benefit equally since the risk was split evenly
The floating-rate payer always benefits since long-term rates tend to rise
Neither side benefits since a swap is designed to be neutral
quiz.explanation: A swap is essentially a zero-sum game between the two parties with respect to interest-rate movement - one side always benefits when rates move in a given direction, the other bears the corresponding disadvantage, which is exactly why the parties have different expectations about future rate direction when they agree to the swap.

quiz.question: Notional VND 200 billion, fixed rate 6%, this period's floating rate 4.5%, half-year term. Who transfers how much?
options: The floating-rate payer transfers VND 1.5 billion to the fixed-rate payer
The fixed-rate payer transfers VND 1.5 billion (= 200 × 1.5% × 0.5 year)
The fixed-rate payer transfers VND 3 billion (= 200 × 1.5%, for the full year)
The two parties exchange the entire VND 200 billion under the contract
quiz.explanation: A 1.5 percentage point gap on VND 200 billion over half a year is VND 1.5 billion, and the fixed-rate payer is the one who owes it since the fixed level is currently higher than floating. Only the difference changes hands, not the notional.

quiz.question: Why does a swap reduce counterparty risk compared with exchanging the full principal?
options: Because a central clearing house guarantees the entire transaction
Because a swap always comes with collateral attached to the contract
Because only the small net difference is actually transferred
Because either side can cancel the contract at any time at no cost
quiz.explanation: A notional of VND 100 billion but net settlement each period of only a few hundred million. If the full principal had to be exchanged both ways, counterparty risk would be hundreds of times larger for the same economic purpose.

quiz.question: A business with a floating-rate loan wants to switch to fixed. How do they set up the swap?
options: Pay off the old loan and take out a new one at a fixed rate
Pay floating and receive fixed from a swap dealer
Pay both fixed and floating, then receive back the difference
Receive floating and pay fixed to a swap dealer
quiz.explanation: The floating leg received exactly cancels out the floating amount owed on the bank loan, leaving only the fixed obligation. The original loan is untouched - that is the main advantage of this approach.

keyTakeaways: Swap: exchanging future cash flows according to an agreed formula
Two most common types: Interest Rate Swap and Currency Swap
The notional principal usually doesn't change hands - only the difference (net) is settled

practicePrompt.question: Two companies agree: each period, Company A pays Company B an amount based on a fixed interest rate of 6%, and B pays A back an amount based on a floating rate (Libor+1%), both calculated on the same notional principal. Neither side transfers that principal amount. What is this transaction called?
options: This is an ordinary bond contract, because it involves fixed and floating interest rates
Swap: exchanging future cash flows according to a formula, settling only the difference
This is an option contract, because Company A has the right to choose whether to perform the transaction or not
This is a futures contract, because the two parties agreed on a trading price in advance
practicePrompt.explanation: Swap: exchanging future cash flows according to an agreed formula. This is an Interest Rate Swap - the notional principal usually doesn't change hands, only the difference (net) between the two interest-rate streams is settled each period.

sections.text: A swap is a derivative contract in which two parties agree to exchange future cash flows according to a predetermined formula. The most common are the Interest Rate Swap (swapping fixed-rate and floating-rate cash flows) and the Currency Swap (swapping cash flows in two different currencies).
Notional principal: a number for calculation, not for changing hands

In an ordinary Interest Rate Swap contract, the notional principal - e.g. VND 100 billion - is usually NOT actually exchanged between the two parties. It is only the basis for calculating the fixed and floating interest each side owes the other. At the end of each period, only the difference (net payment) is actually settled - significantly reducing counterparty risk compared with having to transfer the full notional back and forth.

In a typical Interest Rate Swap - one side pays fixed, one pays floating - this is a zero-sum game between the two parties. If market rates RISE sharply, the side paying fixed (and receiving floating) benefits, since they're paying a fixed level much lower than the new floating rate. If rates FALL, the floating-rate payer (receiving fixed) benefits instead. It is exactly this difference in expectations about future rates that leads the two sides to agree to the swap.

sections.title: Why VND 100 billion notional only sees a few hundred million change hands
sections.equation: Net payment = Notional × (Fixed rate − This period's floating rate)

variables.name: Notional principal
variables.description: Just the basis for multiplying out the interest, doesn't change hands

variables.name: Fixed − Floating
variables.description: Positive means the fixed-rate payer transfers money, negative means the reverse

example.title: Notional VND 100 billion, fixed 5%, this period's floating 4.2%, 6-month term
example.explanation: 0.4% of the notional. If the full VND 100 billion principal had to be exchanged both ways, counterparty risk would be 250 times larger for the exact same economic purpose - that is exactly why the notional stays put.

sections.label: Notional staying put doesn't mean there's no risk
sections.text: What you can actually lose isn't VND 100 billion, but the remaining stream of net payments if your counterparty collapses - plus the cost of signing an equivalent replacement contract at new market rates, usually right when the market has already moved unfavorably. Much smaller than the notional, but not zero.
